summary: A failed ClinicalTrials.gov call must reach the caller as an error, and a fetch that fails partway must hand back what it already collected rather than discarding it.
reason: ctgovCount returns 0 with its error, and many call sites print that number as a study total, so swallowing the error would render a confident zero that reads as 'nothing matched' instead of a broken lookup. ctgovFetch returns its partial results alongside the error on purpose: a scan that dies on page three still gives the caller pages one and two to decide about. A reprint must keep both, and must keep the two scan bounds that go with them - the floor that turns a non-positive maxPages into one page, and the maxStudies cap that stops the scan mid-page. Guarded by TestCountPropagatesTheClientError, TestFetchKeepsPartialResultsOnError, TestFetchTreatsNonPositiveMaxPagesAsOne and TestFetchStopsAtMaxStudies.
validated_outcome: Against the tests that existed before the new file, all four rules survived mutation: dropping the partial results, removing the maxPages floor, removing the maxStudies cap and swallowing the count error each left the package green. Changing the returned count by one failed 3 existing tests as a control. Against the new file all four mutations fail.
